items.heading: Keeping leafy greens and vegetables fresh longer
details: Wrap greens loosely in a dry paper towel and store in a perforated bag in the fridge.
Do not wash vegetables before storing - the extra moisture speeds up spoilage.
Store potatoes and onions separately, in a cool, dark, ventilated place, not the fridge.

items.heading: Preventing brown sugar from hardening
details: Store it with a slice of bread or a marshmallow in an airtight container - it keeps the sugar moist.
If it has already hardened, microwave briefly with a damp paper towel over it, or soften in a low oven for a few minutes.

items.heading: Ripening tomatoes at home
details: Keep them at room temperature, stem side down, away from direct sunlight.
Place them in a paper bag with a banana to speed up ripening.

items.heading: Storing ginger-garlic paste for longer
details: Refrigerate in an airtight jar with a thin layer of oil on top; use within 1-2 weeks.
Freeze in small ice-cube portions for longer storage, up to a few months.

items.heading: Keeping coriander and other herbs fresh
details: Trim the stems and stand them in a glass of water like flowers, covering loosely with a bag, then refrigerate.
Alternatively, wrap in a dry paper towel and store in an airtight box in the fridge.

items.heading: Preventing cut fruit from browning (apple, pear, banana)
details: Toss cut pieces in a bowl of water with a little lemon juice or salt, then drain before serving.

items.heading: Storing rice or flour pest-free
details: Store in airtight containers, and add a few dried neem leaves or a bay leaf to deter pests.
Keep containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.

items.heading: Cooling hot food quickly and safely before refrigerating
details: Divide into smaller, shallow containers to speed up cooling.
Place the container in a larger bowl of cold water or an ice bath, stirring occasionally.
Avoid putting very hot food directly into a packed fridge - leave room for air to circulate.

items.heading: Reheating rice safely
details: Reheat only once, and make sure it is steaming hot all the way through.
Add a splash of water before reheating to prevent it from drying out.
Refrigerate leftover rice within an hour of cooking to reduce the risk of bacteria.
